approachQuestion.prompt:
Exit Readings. For each of two binary trees, read only the leaf labels from left to right. Return whether the two resulting sequences are identical in length and values. Internal labels and grouping do not matter. A leaf has no children; an empty tree yields an empty sequence.

In examples, x(left,right) denotes a node labelled x, and - denotes an absent child. Example 1: Input: A=0(3(-,-),8(5(-,-),-)), B=9(4(3(-,-),5(-,-)),-). Output: true: both leaf sequences are [3,5]. Example 2: Input: A=1(3(-,-),5(-,-)), B=2(5(-,-),3(-,-)). Output: false. Example 3: Input: A=-, B=-. Output: true.

Constraints: combined node count N is at most 200000; labels are signed 32-bit integers and may repeat. The two immutable trees have child pointers only, no cycles or shared nodes, and arbitrary shapes. Return only a Boolean; a traversal iterator may retain its stack between requests.

options.text: Maintain an independent left-first depth-first iterator for each tree. Each request advances that iterator until its next leaf or exhaustion. Compare the two yielded values in lockstep; reject unequal values or unequal exhaustion.
options.feedback: Only leaf order matters. Retaining each iterator’s stack lets comparison continue without restarting or materializing a full sequence.

options.text: Traverse each tree left first, store all leaf labels in separate arrays, then compare those arrays exactly.
options.feedback: It compares the correct sequences for all inputs, but retains their complete contents even though each pair of values can be discarded immediately after comparison.

options.text: Count occurrences of each leaf label in each tree and compare the counts, ignoring order.
options.feedback: Example 2 has identical counts of 3 and 5 but opposite required order.

options.text: Compare nodes at corresponding left and right positions and reject any difference in internal labels or shape.
options.feedback: Example 1 has equal leaf sequences despite different internal labels and grouping, so this would reject a valid pair.

feedback.reason: Compare a filtered traversal lazily; equal leaf sequences do not require equal internal shapes.
details: Each iterator keeps a stack of pending nodes and pushes right before left. To yield, pop until a leaf is found, scheduling children only for non-leaves. Return that leaf value or a distinct exhausted status. Request one value from each iterator, compare, and repeat. Accept only when both are exhausted together. Retain iterator stacks between requests and no leaf history.

Yield leaf values lazily in left-first order and compare corresponding values. Equal prefixes do not suffice: both iterators must exhaust together. Retain iterator stacks between yields to avoid restarting traversals.

“Maintain an independent left-first depth-first iterator for each tree. Each request advances that iterator until its next leaf or exhaustion. Compare the two yielded values in lockstep; reject unequal values or unequal exhaustion.”: Only leaf order matters. Retaining each iterator’s stack lets comparison continue without restarting or materializing a full sequence.

“Traverse each tree left first, store all leaf labels in separate arrays, then compare those arrays exactly.”: It compares the correct sequences for all inputs, but retains their complete contents even though each pair of values can be discarded immediately after comparison.
“Count occurrences of each leaf label in each tree and compare the counts, ignoring order.”: Example 2 has identical counts of 3 and 5 but opposite required order.

“Compare nodes at corresponding left and right positions and reject any difference in internal labels or shape.”: Example 1 has equal leaf sequences despite different internal labels and grouping, so this would reject a valid pair.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the revealed two-iterator method let N>=1 be the combined node count and H=hA+hB, the sum of tree heights in nodes (an empty height is zero). Choose the tight worst-case pair. Count both persistent stacks and current values/statuses; exclude the trees and Boolean result. An exhausted status is distinct from every integer label. Each iterator resumes from its saved frontier, never restarting.
constraints: All legal shapes are allowed; do not assume balance. Heights count nodes, not edges.

Pointer access, comparisons, arithmetic on the stated integer ranges, and allocation/release of a fixed-size frame take constant time. No hashing is used. Count all live explicit frames; the method does not use language recursion or copy paths/subtrees unless explicitly stated.

feedback.reason: Across all yields, visit each node once and retain both active frontiers.
details: Across all yield calls each input node is processed at most once. Both pending depth-first frontiers together use O(hA+hB) space, and deep branching trees can realize that scale.

Each iterator yields exactly the next leaf in left-to-right order. Lockstep equality checks corresponding values and simultaneous exhaustion checks equal length; internal structure is never part of the comparison.

“O(N) time, O(H) auxiliary space”: Across all yield calls each input node is processed at most once. Both pending depth-first frontiers together use O(hA+hB) space, and deep branching trees can realize that scale.
“O(N²) time, O(H) auxiliary space”: Repeated yield calls continue saved traversals; they do not rescan the roots for each leaf.
“O(N) time, O(N) auxiliary space”: This is a looser bound. Neither full leaf sequences nor per-node tables are retained; the tighter bound uses the two heights.
“O(N) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Each iterator retains unresolved sibling nodes, so the working storage is not generally constant.
